title: Anthropic shipped one model twice — safeguards cost it five points
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 — the same model under two safeguard configurations, scoring 55.8% and 60.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 — plus cache reads cut to a quarter. Then a paper arguing on-policy distillation may not distill at all, and Dan Luu's scorecard on Ed Zitron's AI predictions.

threads.name: Frontier-model release gating
threads.status: OpenAI says Astra is the first of its models to meet its critical cybersecurity threshold and plans to ship it soon with limited access to the strongest cyber capabilities; Anthropic simultaneously shipped one model in two safeguard configurations and published a score for each.
threads.arc: Gating has moved from a release/no-release decision to a graded product line — different rulebooks over the same weights, with the capability difference now visible in a benchmark table.

dives.story: Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1: same weights, two safeguard configurations
dives.why_it_matters: Anyone buying or deploying frontier models now has a published, if uncontrolled, number for what safeguards cost in capability, plus a cache-read price cut and an effort dial that changes the cost of a single agent call by more than an order of magnitude.
Teams paying to run a large teacher model inside a post-training loop can cheaply test whether the teacher's dense token scores are doing anything a fixed negative advantage wouldn't.

dives.story: Dan Luu's scorecard on Ed Zitron's AI predictions
dives.why_it_matters: Practitioners and executives calibrating on public AI commentary get a rare falsifiable audit of a prominent forecaster — and a reminder that grading a critic's dated predictions says nothing about whether the underlying economic argument holds.

concepts_taught: on-policy distillation as dense token-level supervision: the student generates, the teacher scores its own off-distribution text, and why that off-policy scoring is noisy — noisier as the teacher scales — such that a fixed negative advantage on low-probability tokens matches teacher supervision

lore.note: Alan admitted on air that in February 2024 he privately thought AI progress was near its ceiling — he looked at scaling curves and the data situation and concluded it would flatten inside a year — and says the only reason he isn't on a scorecard is that he never published it. He refuses to claim anything changed his mind; he was wrong and the world kept going. His practice since: write down what would falsify a call at the same time he makes it, in the same place — 'the difference between a forecast and a mood.'
